title: How the US anti–data-center movement can learn from Ireland to New Zealand
dek: Writer Paris Marx, author of Hyperscale, says long-term international experience offers lessons for U.S. campaigns against data center construction.
body:
Paris Marx, who wrote the book Hyperscale and has tracked global data center development for years, argues that activists and policymakers in the United States can learn from what has happened in other countries, including Ireland and New Zealand.

## Why it matters

Data center construction and expansion are drawing local and national attention in the U.S. The broader pattern of development, the political responses to it, and the outcomes from other countries could offer practical guidance for U.S. actors, according to Marx. Understanding those foreign experiences could shape how communities, regulators, and legislators respond here. Specific policy prescriptions or outcomes from abroad were not detailed in the material provided.

## The details

- Paris Marx is the author of Hyperscale and has been tracking data center development around the world for years.
- Marx’s reporting and analysis point to lessons from multiple countries, with Ireland and New Zealand singled out as cases of interest.
- The argument presented is that the U.S. movement against data centers has much to learn from international examples.
- The exact lessons, which policies worked or failed in those countries, and how directly they apply to U.S. contexts were not specified in the summary material.

## What to watch

Watch for more reporting from Marx and others that lays out the concrete policies, regulatory approaches, and community strategies used abroad, and for U.S. localities to reference or adapt those examples. Also look for follow-up analysis that compares outcomes across jurisdictions so practitioners can judge what is transferable and what is specific to local conditions.

Source: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/what-the-us-anti-data-center-movement-can-learn-from-everywhere-else/)
